title: Pannonia
fact_summary: The old Roman name for the land west of the Danube in today's Hungary. In the sources on this map it goes from a Frankish border province to the Hungarians' home.

claims.text: The Annals of Fulda say that in 894 the Hungarians destroyed “the whole of Pannonia”, and that in 896 the emperor gave Pannonia to his duke Brazlavo to defend.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

claims.text: Under 900 the same annals say the Hungarians returned from Bavaria “to their own, into Pannonia”.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

claims.text: Widukind says the Avars, after ravaging their neighbours, “at last began to live in Pannonia”.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

claims.text: The edition of Thietmar calls Waic (Stephen) “rex Pannonicus”, king of Pannonia.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the edition's index says.

claims.text: A 2024 genetic study says the former Pannonian provinces, “i.e., Transdanubia (corresponding to the territory of today's Western Hungary)”, became part of the Carolingian Empire after the Avar realm broke up.
claims.certainty_reason: The study's summary of the history, not its own finding.

open_questions.text: Between 894 and 900 Pannonia changes, in one set of annals, from a land the Hungarians destroy to the land they go home to. What happened in those six years?

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
